guide.a.what_is_a_domain_name:
A domain name is the address people type into a browser to reach a website. For example tickets.example.co.uk.

Your site already works at a long address it was given when it was built. A domain name is a shorter address that you buy and point at your site, so people can find you more easily.
guide.q.where_do_i_buy_a_domain_name: Where do I buy a domain name?
guide.a.where_do_i_buy_a_domain_name:
You buy one from a company that sells domain names. Well-known sellers are Cloudflare, Namecheap, and GoDaddy, but any seller will do. A web designer can also buy one for you.

A domain name usually costs between £5 and £20 a year, and you pay every year to keep it. When you buy, you only buy the name. You do not need to buy anything else — no website space or hosting — because this site already runs on the internet. The name just needs to point at it.
guide.q.setup_custom_domain: How do I set up a custom domain?
guide.a.setup_custom_domain:
First you need a domain name you have bought. Read Where do I buy a domain name? above if you do not have one yet.

  1. Open Advanced settings and find the Custom domain section. If you cannot see the section, ask the company that runs this site for you to turn it on.
  2. Type your domain name, for example tickets.example.co.uk, and save.
  3. The page shows you a CNAME record to add. A CNAME record is one line in the settings of the company you bought your domain name from. It tells that company to send everyone who types your domain name to this site. Copy the details from this page into your domain seller's settings page. Every seller has one, usually called DNS settings.
  4. Come back and click Validate custom domain.

Validation can take a few minutes. A brand-new domain name can take up to a day to start working everywhere.
guide.a.what_does_validation_do:
Validation checks that your domain name really points at this site.

When the check passes, this site also gets a free security certificate for your domain name. The certificate turns on HTTPS — the padlock symbol in the browser's address bar. It means the connection between a visitor and your site is private.

You can validate again at any time, for example after you change your domain seller's settings.
guide.a.what_if_validation_fails:
Validation runs when you save your domain. If it fails, your domain is still saved.

The page explains why it failed. The usual reason is that the CNAME record has not spread everywhere yet. Think of it like a letter that has been posted but not delivered. Add the CNAME record shown on the page if you have not already, wait a few minutes (up to a day for a new name), then click Validate custom domain again.

Until validation works, ticket links, redirects, and emails keep using your other address — your host subdomain, or the long address the site started with. That address keeps working.
guide.q.which_domain_is_used_for_ticket_: Which address is used for ticket links and emails?
guide.a.which_domain_is_used_for_ticket_:
This site puts one address on the links it makes — ticket links, QR codes, redirects, and emails. It uses the first address on this list that is ready:

  1. Your custom domain, once it has passed validation. Saving it is not enough on its own.
  2. Your host subdomain, if you have one.
  3. The long address the site started with. On Bunny, that address ends in b-cdn.net or bunny.run.

A host subdomain and a validated custom domain both keep working for visitors. Only the highest one on the list is used for links the site makes.
guide.a.available_settings:
The Settings page (owners only) lets you set up:

  • Business email — the address where you receive messages about bookings, and the address attendees can reply to
  • Payment provider — Stripe, Square, SumUp, or none
  • Booking fee — an extra percentage added to ticket prices (needs a payment provider)
  • Header image — a logo or banner shown at the top of every page
  • Embed hosts — limits which websites can show your booking forms
  • Terms and conditions — rules attendees must agree to before booking
  • Features — turn the public site and other tools on or off
  • Site theme — light or dark
  • Admin password — change your login password

Your country is chosen once, during set-up, and sets your timezone, currency, and phone prefix. It cannot be changed here afterwards.
guide.q.how_does_the_header_image_work: How does the header image work?
guide.a.how_does_the_header_image_work:
Upload a logo or banner from Settings and it appears at the top of every page.

When your booking form is shown inside another website, the image is hidden. That website already shows its own branding.

You can use JPEG, PNG, or WebP pictures, up to 256 KB in size. Uploading a new image replaces the old one, and the Remove Image button clears it completely. The picture is stored scrambled, and each visitor's browser keeps a copy so it only downloads once.

If the section is missing, your host has not turned on image storage. Ask them to set up a Bunny storage zone for your site.
guide.a.advanced_settings:
The main Settings page links to Advanced Settings for less common set-up. Advanced settings include:

  • Public API — let other websites read your listings and take bookings (for your web builder)
  • Apple Wallet and Google Wallet — add tickets to phones' wallet apps
  • Email provider — choose and set up the company that sends your emails
  • Email templates — change the words in confirmation and notification emails
  • Host subdomain — a free address for your site, when your host offers it
  • Custom domain — use a domain name you bought
  • Backups — save and download copies of everything on your site
  • Software updates — check for and install new versions
  • Database reset — delete everything and start fresh
guide.a.what_is_debug_page:
The debug page at /admin/debug shows at a glance which services are set up (payments, email, wallets, storage, notifications, database) and which are missing. It never shows secret keys. Use it when something does not work — it tells you where to look.

The page also lists every system limit (file sizes, how long links stay valid, login lock-out times, and so on) with its normal value and its current value. Your host can change a limit with an environment variable — a setting stored outside the site. Changed limits are highlighted. A table at the bottom shows when each kind of old data was last cleaned up.
guide.a.what_is_the_debug_footer:
The debug footer is a small line at the bottom of every admin page you look at while signed in. It says how long the page took to build and how much database work it took.

Click the line to open it. You see every database question the page asked, how long each one took, and what was saved from earlier answers. Visitors never see this footer — it appears only on admin pages while you are signed in.

Use it to find slow pages without leaving the page you are on.
guide.a.what_are_built_sites: The Built Sites page (owners only) is a list of Tickets sites you have made with this system. Each entry records the site's name and its web address. You can add, change, and delete entries to keep track of every site you look after.
guide.q.how_do_i_create_a_new_tickets: How do I make a new Tickets site?
guide.a.how_do_i_create_a_new_tickets:
This one is for the person who set up your sites. Everyone else can skip it.

Visit /admin/builder to make a brand-new site. Enter a site name, a database address (libsql format), and a database token. The builder fetches the newest code from GitHub, creates the site on Bunny, fills in the secrets (including a new encryption key), tests the database, and publishes the site. Set-up like email, wallets, and storage is copied from this site automatically.
guide.q.what_do_i_need_before_building_a: What do I need before making a site?
guide.a.what_do_i_need_before_building_a: You need a libsql database — for example a free one from Turso — with its address and token. The server also needs BUNNY_API_KEY set. Only owners can use the builder.
guide.q.can_i_add_a_site_record_without: Can I add a site to the list without using the builder?
guide.a.can_i_add_a_site_record_without: Yes. On the Built Sites page, click Add Built Site and type the site's name and address. Use this to keep track of sites you made another way.
guide.q.what_happens_when_a_site_plan: What happens when a site plan sells with no site available?
guide.a.what_happens_when_a_site_plan:
The booking and its payment stand, but the buyer gets no site yet.

When email is set up, you get a warning email at your business email address. The owner's log records the problem either way. The buyer's attendee page also shows No site assigned yet on the plan's row.

To fix it, add or build sites on the Built Sites page. Then send the notification again for each buyer from their attendee page. The resend gives them a site, and emails them the set-up link when email is set up.
guide.q.how_do_i_register_a_subdomain: How do I register a subdomain?
guide.a.how_do_i_register_a_subdomain:
1. Open Advanced settings and find the Host subdomain section.
  2. Type the name you want. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
  3. Click Check if the name is free to see your full site address.
  4. Tick the box to confirm the registration.
  5. Click Register subdomain.

The subdomain is free, and you do not need to change anything at a domain seller. Once you register it, you cannot change the name.
guide.a.what_is_host_subdomain:
A host subdomain is a free, shorter address for your site. It replaces the long address the site starts with.

You pick the first part of the name. The host — the company that runs this site for you — sets the ending. Press Check if the name is free on the settings page to see your full site address. Once you register the name, you cannot change it. The section appears only when your host offers subdomains.
guide.q.can_i_use_both_a_subdomain_and: Can I use both a subdomain and a custom domain?
guide.a.can_i_use_both_a_subdomain_and: Yes. Your host subdomain and custom domain can both work at the same time. People can reach your site through either address.
